articles.headline: Argenx sees unusual setback with failure of late-stage study of drug for autoimmune disease
articles.summary: Argenx reported that Vyvgart (efgartigimod) failed to beat placebo in a Phase 3 trial for Sjögren's disease, an unexpected and significant miss given the drug's prior commercial success across other autoimmune indications. The failure is described as unusual for a drug with Vyvgart's track record and removes a meaningful TAM expansion opportunity that Wall Street had been pricing in. The setback compounds earlier pipeline disappointments and raises questions about the limits of FcRn inhibition as a platform across autoimmune diseases.
articles.why_it_matters: The Phase 3 failure narrows Vyvgart's peak sales ceiling and is an actionable negative catalyst for ARGX longs, while also serving as a competitive read-through for other FcRn inhibitor developers such as Johnson & Johnson and UCB.

articles.headline: McKinsey: The AI-powered future of care
articles.summary: McKinsey examines how AI is transforming clinical workflows, patient engagement, and care delivery across health systems, distinguishing where ROI is materializing from where it remains aspirational. The research synthesizes cross-industry evidence to map which AI applications in healthcare are proving durable versus hype-driven. It offers a framework for evaluating digital health and AI-enabled care companies on their ability to capture lasting value.
articles.why_it_matters: For investors evaluating health tech SaaS, diagnostics AI, and AI-enabled care platforms, this McKinsey framework helps separate structurally advantaged adopters from companies riding temporary enthusiasm — directly relevant to competitive moat and deep business diligence.
